headline: Funding flows. Procurement reshuffles. Startups scramble.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and procurement shifts, signaling evolving dynamics in the aerospace sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster their capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are increasingly critical for national security. The Department of Defense's interest in such technologies is becoming a cash cow for startups.
stories.soWhat: The DoD's push for co-orbital security means True Anomaly isn't just riding the wave; they're steering the ship.

stories.head: Space Force reorganizes with nine new portfolios
stories.body: The Space Force has completed a significant procurement reorganization, establishing nine new acquisition portfolios to streamline decision-making. This shift aims to enhance responsiveness across major mission areas, reflecting a growing recognition that agility is key in modern defense operations. Expect to see faster procurement cycles as a result.
stories.soWhat: When it comes to defense procurement, speed is the new black; this reorg could reshape how contracts are awarded.

stories.head: Pulse Space lands $40M for laser power tech
stories.body: Pulse Space has been awarded $40 million by the Space Force to develop laser systems designed to transmit power and data between spacecraft. This funding highlights a growing interest in laser technology as a means of enhancing spacecraft capabilities, which could redefine operational paradigms in space logistics.
stories.soWhat: If lasers can power spacecraft, we might need to rethink everything we thought we knew about space energy.

watchlist.title: Space Force's procurement strategy unfolds
watchlist.body: The new acquisition portfolios could lead to faster contract awards, affecting a range of companies vying for Space Force contracts.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
